title: The 'Digital Arrest' Fake Police Video Call
titleMr: 'डिजिटल अरेस्ट' आणि बनावट पोलीस व्हिडिओ कॉल
summary: Scammers pose as CBI or Mumbai Cyber Police officers over WhatsApp/Skype video calls, claiming your Aadhaar was found in a drug parcel or money laundering case, and force you onto continuous video camera supervision until you transfer money.
summaryMr: बनावट पोलीस अधिकारी बनकर अंमली पदार्थ किंवा मनी लाँड्रिंगच्या केसची भीती दाखवून पैशांची उकळत करणे.
howItWorks: You receive an IVR phone call claiming your courier (FedEx/DHL) contains illegal passports or drugs.
The call is transferred to a fake 'Police Officer' wearing a realistic uniform sitting in a background decorated with official seals.
The fraudster threatens immediate arrest under PMLA/NDPS and orders you to stay on video call ('Digital Arrest') without contacting anyone.
You are forced to transfer all your savings into 'RBI Clearance Accounts' or 'Secret Verification Accounts' to prove innocence.
redFlags: Police or CBI demanding money transfer to prove innocence.
Insisting on continuous video camera surveillance on Skype/WhatsApp.
Threatening that notifying family will result in immediate jail.
realWorldFact: Law Enforcement agencies (Police, CBI, ED, Narcotics Bureau) NEVER conduct 'Digital Arrests' or demand money transfers over video calls. Any video call demanding money is 100% fake.

title: The 'Like YouTube Videos & Earn' Task Scam
titleMr: युट्यूब व्हिडिओ लाईक करा आणि कमवा' टास्क फसवणूक
summary: Victims are recruited on WhatsApp/Telegram for easy work-from-home tasks. After paying a small initial reward, scammers lure them into depositing lakhs under 'Prepaid Crypto Tasks'.
summaryMr: घरी बसून युट्यूब लाईक्स किंवा रेटिंग देऊन रोज हजारो रुपये कमवण्याचे बनावट आमिष.
howItWorks: Unsolicited WhatsApp message offering Rs 150 per YouTube video liked.
You complete 3 simple likes and actually receive Rs 450 in your UPI account to build extreme trust.
You are added to a Telegram group with 50+ members (mostly fake bot accounts posting false profit screenshots).
You are instructed to join 'Prepaid VIP Tasks' where depositing Rs 10,000 promises Rs 15,000 return.
When you try to withdraw your profits, the admin claims your 'score dropped' and demands Rs 50,000 more.
redFlags: Unsolicited job offers from international WhatsApp numbers (+63, +62).
Requirement to deposit your own money to unlock earned salary.
realWorldFact: No legitimate marketing company asks job seekers to deposit money into personal accounts to receive task commissions.

title: The 'Electricity Bill Unpaid - Power Cut Tonight' APK Trap
titleMr: लाईट बिल थकबाकी व विजेचे कनेक्शन तोडण्याची भीती दाखवणारी ॲप फसवणूक
summary: An urgent SMS claims your electricity bill is unpaid and power will be cut at 9:30 PM tonight. Clicking the link downloads an APK app that drains your bank account.
summaryMr: वीज बिल न भरल्यास आज रात्री वीज खंडित होईल असा मेसेज पाठवून ॲप डाऊनलोड करायला लावणे.
howItWorks: SMS arrives: 'Dear Consumer your electricity power will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 pm from MSEDCL officer. Call immediately.'
You call the provided number in panic; the caller asks you to pay Rs 10 via a special app link sent on WhatsApp.
The link installs a malicious .apk app file (disguised as 'MSEDCL Bill Update').
The app reads your banking OTPs in the background and clears out your savings.
redFlags: SMS coming from personal 10-digit phone numbers instead of official Telecom Sender IDs (like VM-MSEDCL).
Requests to download apps directly via WhatsApp file attachments.
Threats of power disconnection within hours.
realWorldFact: MSEDCL and electricity distribution boards never send SMS from personal numbers or ask users to download third-party APK files.

title: The 'Army Officer OLX Bike/Car' Advance Token Trick
summary: Fraudsters post ads for cars, bikes, or furniture at half price, posing as transferred Army officers who demand advance military gate pass fees before delivery.
summaryMr: सैन्य दलात असल्याचा खोटा ओळखपत्र दाखवून अर्ध्या किंमतीत गाडी देण्याच्या नावाने अॅडव्हान्स उकळणे.
howItWorks: Ad on OLX offers a 2022 Royal Enfield or Swift car for an unbelievably cheap price.
Seller sends a photo of a forged Army ID card and canteen card to establish immediate trust.
Seller claims the vehicle is parked at the Army Cantonment Gate and requires Rs 3,500 'Army Gate Pass / Courier Charges' via UPI before releasing it.
Once money is sent, the scammer asks for Rs 10,000 more or switches off the phone.
redFlags: Refusal to meet in person to show the vehicle before taking money.
Sending QR codes claiming 'scan this to receive advance payment'.
realWorldFact: Indian Armed Forces personnel do not use official military identity cards for commercial sales on classified apps.
